items.title: Anat Cohen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 9, 2021
items.q: And you know my friend Jovino Santos Neto he is a great musician

ctx.x: I’m remembering the thing you said about the Latin band in Boston and that you learned to move to the music and it gave me this flash like when I’ve tried to listen to Latin music sometimes I get aggravated, like I lose “one.” And I’m wondering if moving like that helps like keep one in your head.

You know that’s always, what you’re describing is always that conflict between the feeling and the thinking. Because what you feel is what you feel and nobody can argue with you. It’s always right, that’s what you feel. Now whether one person calls it “one” and another person calls it “four” that’s a whole other question and that’s when you want to write music or analyze music then maybe you need to know where is “one.” But the feeling is the feeling so there is first that. But it was not a natural thing for me…

Do you have hopes for what your audience is absorbing from your music? There’s things that happen onstage that you and musicians in general think oh that was a wonderful moment. Or if you write a melody, I’m trying to form this question about what do you think your audience is hearing in contrast to what you’re hearing?
